recognize_zh: 中央一顆小型淋巴樣細胞，胞質極少、只剩薄薄一層，染色質均勻濃縮且平滑、不見核仁，形狀受周圍紅血球擠壓成多角形，符合血原母細胞（hematogone）；右側為分葉嗜中性球，左下為小型晚期紅血球母細胞。
features: Small lymphoid cell only slightly larger than a red cell, molded into a polygonal shape
Extremely scant, barely visible rim of pale cytoplasm
Homogeneous, smooth condensed chromatin with faint linear streaks
Nearby segmented neutrophil and a small orthochromatic erythroblast with dense pyknotic nucleus in the lower left
describe_en: Smear shows a small lymphoid cell with an extremely high N:C ratio, a barely perceptible rim of cytoplasm and homogeneous smooth condensed chromatin without nucleoli, molded by adjacent red cells. A segmented neutrophil and an orthochromatic erythroblast are also present. The cell has the morphology of a hematogone (normal B-lymphocyte precursor); because hematogones overlap morphologically with lymphoblasts, flow cytometric maturation pattern analysis is needed when they are numerous.

ddx.vs: Lymphoblasts tend to be larger with finer, more dispersed chromatin and occasional nucleoli, and show an aberrant maturation-arrested immunophenotype on flow cytometry.
Erythroblasts have a round, very dense pyknotic nucleus surrounded by hemoglobinized orange-pink cytoplasm, as seen in the lower left cell.
Mature lymphocytes have coarser, clumped chromatin and slightly more visible blue cytoplasm and lack CD10/CD34/TdT.
